list.text: A rule can be found that returns the beat itself, not its bar or its half.
list.evidence: The candidate won on two synthetic held-out sets (94 to 95%) but lost on 12 tracks with tapped labels: 7 exact against 9 for the old rule. Which level is the beat turned out to be the listener's choice (issue #15).

list.text: The listener's beat is one level of the metrical ladder (pre-registered: at least 11 of 12 tapped tracks, 95% of held-out grooves).
list.evidence: 12 of 12 tapped tracks; 96.5% on both held-out groove sets; all 120 noise controls empty (issue #29).

list.text: The ladder tells a bar of 3 from a bar of 2 better than always answering 2 (pre-registered: at least 70%).
list.evidence: 88.8% against 62.9%, and 95.5% against 73.1%, on two held-out groove sets (issue #29).

list.text: On live musicians the ladder holds the tapped beat on at least 80% of tracks.
list.evidence: Pre-registered on 2026-11-22 for 17 live recordings: bands, a folk festival, 1923 jazz, a work song. Waiting for the taps.

list.text: On free improvisation and on room noise the ladder stays empty.
list.evidence: Pre-registered on 2026-11-22: a violin improvisation, a taksim soundcheck, and 19 s of festival room sound. Waiting for the taps.

list.text: On a crooked Bulgarian dance (krivo horo) the ladder finds no grouping by 2 or by 3 above the beat: it says nothing rather than a wrong meter.
list.evidence: Written on 2026-11-25, before any tap or run on it. Waiting for the taps.
